reset.topicPlaceholder: No client is connected, so enter the topic
reset.timeInvalid: That is not a valid time
reset.note: RocketMQ resets by time, not by offset: the broker finds the first message stored at or after that moment, per queue. “Earliest” is the oldest message still retained — anything older has rolled off the commit log.
reset.risky: This moves the read position and can replay or skip messages

clone.title: Clone consume offsets
clone.fromOffline: Read stored offsets (source group is shut down)
clone.risky: Overwrites the target group's current positions
clone.note: Writes the target group the source's exact per-queue offsets, so a replacement group does not replay what the old one handled. Unlike a reset, which finds a position by time, this copies positions.

reuse.connectionsNote: One set for every protocol; only the connection form's fields follow the protocol (3a)
reuse.dataPagesPage: Overview · topics · message query · send · consumer groups · dead letters · nodes
reuse.dataPagesNote: One page skeleton plus a per-protocol field mapping, trimmed by the 3h matrix (e.g. 3c→4c)
reuse.amqpNote: An AMQP-only model with its own navigation and pages (4a); the table and sheet primitives are still shared
reuse.mqttPage: MQTT topic tree + live subscription workbench

reuse.pulsarNote: A tenant / namespace cascade above the topics page; the rest is the Kafka view
reuse.redisNote: A PEL (pending entries) table and XCLAIM actions inside the consumer-groups page
reuse.title: Page reuse strategy
reuse.subtitle: The frontend renders from a protocol adapter plus its capabilities: experience first, reuse second (read with the 3h capability matrix)
reuse.advice: Suggested implementation: one adapter per protocol exposing a single interface plus a capabilities description; pages render their fields and actions from those capabilities, and a separate module gets its own protocol route.

nav.title: Navigation model
nav.subtitle: Three layers and where they are isolated: window → connection tab → page. Tabs share no state; drag one out for a new window, or set two side by side to compare.
nav.windowA: Window A (more than one can be open)
nav.pageLayer: Page layer: each tab keeps its own sidebar position, filters, scroll and query results
nav.tearOff: Drag a tab out → window B
nav.sideBySide: Two tabs side by side → split compare
nav.sideBySideNote: Check backlog and messages on both sides during a migration or dual write
nav.isolation: Isolated: page state · query cache · refresh timers · credential sessions · alert subscriptions. Shared: settings · the connection library · the notification centre.
